name: Lab Baseline Coverage
description: Detection gap analysis for the Week 1 lab (Ubuntu server, Windows 10 VM). Blue = logs collected, no tested detection. Green = search or rule tested on test data. Red = no log source collected centrally. Each technique comment names the evidence and the data it was tested on.

techniques.comment: Splunk search 1 on own auth.log (failed SSH logins by user and IP). Wazuh custom rule 100102 fires on more than 5 LOGIN_FAILED in 60s. Windows 4625 collected by the Wazuh agent. Account-lockout search (7) returned 0 events, so it is not counted.
Splunk search 9 flagged an off-hours SSH login on own auth.log. Tested with one real event.
Splunk search 6 (PowerShell EIDs 800/4103). Validated on the TryHackMe windowslogs dataset. The lab's own Windows feed does not yet collect the PowerShell or Sysmon channels.
Splunk search 3 (suspicious parent process): WmiPrvSE.exe spawning net.exe. Validated on the TryHackMe dataset. Own Sysmon log is not collected centrally.
Splunk search 5: two internal hosts sent more than 100 MB to one external IP. Tested on a synthetic firewall log generated by script, so volumes are inflated.
Windows System 7045 would show it. Splunk search 2 returned 0 events on the dataset; the event was only confirmed at source on CSLAB1. No alert exists.
Windows 4720 (user account created) is collected; 2 events seen on the windows10 VM. No alert built.
Splunk search 10 (group changes 4728/4729/4732) returned add/remove events on the TryHackMe data but no change to a privileged group. 4732 confirmed at source on CSLAB1. No tested alert.
auditd 'cron' key watches cron files and syslog records cron runs. No alert built.
nginx access log collected via Filebeat and Logstash. No detection rule for exploitation patterns.
Windows 4624 logon events are collected; logon type 10 would indicate RDP. No detection built.
Splunk search 8 (top source IPs) ran on the synthetic firewall log, but every source touched 6 ports so it did not separate scanners. No tested detection.
No email gateway, mailbox or message-trace logs are collected.
Needs Sysmon EID 10 (process access to lsass.exe). Sysmon is installed but its log is not collected centrally.
Needs Sysmon EID 13 (registry value set). Sysmon is installed but its log is not collected centrally.
No share-access auditing (Security 5140/5145) enabled and no network flow logs.
No proxy, web gateway or egress logs, so uploads to web services are invisible.
Sysmon EID 22 (DNS) stays on the endpoint. Splunk search 4 ran only on the TryHackMe dataset and its 'rare' flags were noise from a tiny sample.
No VPN or remote-access gateway logs are collected.

legendItems.label: Green: detection (search or rule tested on test data; see comment for data source)
Blue: visibility only (logs collected, no tested detection)
Red: blind spot (no log source collected centrally)
